title: Influence Cauchy--Schwarz inequality
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube. Then $I(f)^2\le n\sum_iI_i(f)^2$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n (f : {0,1}^n → ℝ)
n is the arity / number of coordinates appearing as the multiplier on the right
replaced:
The total influence obeys
\[
  I[f]^2 \;\le\; n \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]^2 .
\]
